# Northstar — Monday Business Review Analysis

---

## 1. EXECUTIVE SUMMARY

**Total ARR has declined.** Northstar entered October with approximately €8.96M in ARR across 35 active customers. Five customers churned during October (1 Mid-market, 4 SMB), taking €303,600 in ARR with them. New logos and expansions have not yet fully offset this loss at the current-run-rate level.

**The plans data overstates October performance.** The plans.csv counts all customers invoiced during October, including those that churned mid-month. On an end-of-month basis, effective MRR declined from ~€746K to ~€732K — a loss of ~€14K, or -1.8%.

**Enterprise plan margins are compressing.** Revenue is flat at ~€660K MRR but infrastructure and support costs are both climbing, pushing gross margin from 32.2% to 29.5% in one month.

**Soylent (€234K ARR) is an urgent retention risk.** Usage fell 27%, support ticket volume nearly tripled (including a critical-severity ticket), and billing was recently reduced. If lost, this would be the largest single customer churn since the data period began.

**We cannot answer the CFO's CAC payback question.** No channel spend data is available, and trial-to-paid conversion is not tracked. This is a hard blocker, not an analytical gap.

**Recommendation:** Do not cut the SMB segment wholesale — cut selectively by plan. Do not increase paid_search spend without cost data. Prioritise engineering investment in the **Pro plan** where rate-limit friction is driving support load and may have contributed to Nakatomi's churn.

---

## 2. REVENUE & CUSTOMER HEALTH

### 2a. MRR Bridge — What Actually Happened in October

| Item | MRR impact |
|---|---|
| September ending MRR (all active customers) | ~€746,100 |
| Nakatomi churn (Pro, Oct 19) | −€15,000 |
| 4× Starter churns (slate-rock, mega-lo, dinoco, buy-n-large) | −€10,300 |
| Soylent rate adjustment | −€2,500 |
| Hooli expansion (booked Sep, effective Oct) | +€3,000 |
| 5× new logos (spacely, cogswell, bishop, gekko, paper-street) | +€11,100 |
| **October ending MRR** | **~€732,400** |
| **Net MRR change** | **−€13,700 (−1.8%)** |

> Note: the plans.csv reports October MRR as €757,700. That figure includes five customers who churned during October but were still invoiced. It does not represent the true run-rate entering November.

### 2b. ARR Summary

| | Start of Oct | End of Oct | Change |
|---|---|---|---|
| Enterprise segment (8 customers) | €6,780,000 | €6,780,000 | — |
| Mid-market (10 → 9 active) | €1,710,000 | €1,530,000 | −€180,000 |
| SMB (18 → 14 active) | €602,400 | €478,800 | −€123,600 |
| **Total** | **€9,092,400** | **€8,788,800** | **−€303,600 (−3.3%)** |

Pending expansion bookings (stark +€84K, umbrella +€48K, globex +€42K, massive-dynamic +€18K, cyberdyne +€24K = **+€216K**) will take effect in November's billing cycle. Once booked, total ARR would recover to ~€9,004,800 — modestly above the October start. However, this depends on those expansions actually billing, and the churned ARR is permanently lost.

### 2c. Churn Detail

All five October churns were customers with **declining usage and unresolved support issues**:

| Customer | Segment | Plan | ARR lost | Usage Δ (Sep→Oct) | Support pattern |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Nakatomi | Mid-market | Pro | €180,000 | −16.1% | High-severity api_errors ticket was **open** at churn |
| Slate-rock | SMB | Starter | €24,000 | −34.7% | High api_errors ticket was open going into Oct |
| Mega-lo-mart | SMB | Starter | €32,400 | −37.1% | Low billing ticket pending |
| Dinoco | SMB | Starter | €27,600 | −35.5% | Escalated from low billing (Sep) to high api_errors (Oct) |
| Buy-n-large | SMB | Starter | €39,600 | −37.0% | Low billing ticket pending |

The Starter churns share two traits: sharp usage declines (34–37%) and billing-related support tickets. This suggests price sensitivity or value dissatisfaction. The Nakatomi churn is more concerning — it is a mid-market Pro customer lost with a high-severity ticket unresolved.

### 2d. Soylent — Retention Risk Alert

Soylent is the clearest near-term churn risk in the portfolio:

- **Usage:** dropped 27% (980K → 715K requests; 56 → 41 active users)
- **Support:** 3 tickets in September → 8 in October, including 1 critical-severity and 3 high-severity (one still open)
- **Billing:** September invoice was €22,000 but current ARR implies €19,500/mo; October invoice matched the lower rate — suggesting a recent concession
- **Duplicate invoice:** INV-2026-10-0209 appears twice (stripe + billing_sync, each €19,500). If both settle, Soylent is overbilled by €19,500, which would further damage the relationship.

Soylent represents €234,000 ARR. Losing it would be the single largest churn event in this dataset.

### 2e. Near-Term Renewal Exposure

Wayne Enterprises (€1,008,000 ARR, 2nd-largest customer) renews **30 November 2026** — less than two months away. Usage is healthy (+10%) but the customer has 4 high-severity support tickets across Sep–Oct (api_errors and performance), with 2 currently open/pending. This renewal must be actively managed.

---

## 3. ACQUISITION

### 3a. New Logos by Channel

| Channel | Sep new logos | Sep attributed ARR | Oct new logos | Oct attributed ARR | Total |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Partner | 2 | €166,800 | 0 | €0 | €166,800 |
| Content | 1 | €45,600 | 2 | €45,600 | €91,200 |
| Outbound | 1 | €33,600 | 1 | €22,800 | €56,400 |
| Paid search | 0 | €0 | 2 | €64,800 | €64,800 |
| **Total** | **4** | **€246,000** | **5** | **€133,200** | **€379,200** |

Partner drove the highest-value new logos in September (vandelay at €132K) but had zero new logos in October. Paid search was the only channel to generate expansion bookings (stark +€84K, umbrella +€48K, globex +€42K in October alone).

### 3b. Expansion Bookings by Channel

| Channel | Sep expansions | Oct expansions | Total attributed |
|---|---|---|---|
| Paid search | €36,000 (hooli) | €174,000 (stark, umbrella, globex) | €210,000 |
| Content | — | €18,000 (massive-dynamic) | €18,000 |
| Outbound | — | €24,000 (cyberdyne) | €24,000 |
| **Total** | **€36,000** | **€216,000** | **€252,000** |

> Important caveat: expansion attribution is typically last-touch. We cannot conclude that paid_search *caused* these expansions — they may reflect organic account growth that happened to be attributed to the most recent paid touch. This is an attribution limitation, not evidence of channel effectiveness.

### 3c. Funnel: Lead → Trial (Not Lead → Paid)

| Channel | Sep leads | Sep trials | Sep trial rate | Oct leads | Oct trials | Oct trial rate |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Paid search | 520 | 44 | 8.5% | 900 | 58 | 6.4% |
| Content | 260 | 31 | 11.9% | 330 | 34 | 10.3% |
| Partner | 60 | 15 | 25.0% | 75 | 17 | 22.7% |
| Outbound | 160 | 10 | 6.3% | 195 | 11 | 5.6% |

Paid search lead volume nearly doubled (520 → 900) but trial conversion deteriorated (8.5% → 6.4%), suggesting lead quality is falling as spend scales. Partner has the best trial rate by far but very low volume.

### 3d. What Cannot Be Concluded

1. **CAC and CAC payback are impossible to calculate.** The data pack contains no channel spend data (ad spend, sales costs, agency fees). Without cost, there is no CAC. The CFO's request cannot be fulfilled with this data.

2. **Trial-to-paid conversion is not tracked.** The funnel stops at trial. We cannot close the loop from trial to revenue.

3. **Channel ROI cannot be determined.** We see attributed revenue but not cost. A channel with high attributed revenue might also have high cost, making it the least efficient.

4. **The apparent paid_search expansion "success" may be an attribution artefact.** Three large enterprise customers (stark, umbrella, globex) expanded in October with paid_search as the attributed channel. These are mature accounts (customer since 2023–2024). Their expansion likely reflects organic growth, not a paid campaign response.
